chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'And it will be said: Who is a caster (of spells)?' and he thinks it is the separation.
For that is the son of Adam when death comes upon him; he says, 'Is there a physician?'
He is convinced of the separation from his loved ones.
And the calf binds to the calf; the world binds to the Hereafter.
Then to your Lord on that day is the driving.
He said: The return is to the Lord of the worlds.

key_terms.السَّاقُ: Calf (of the leg), used metaphorically for the world or the body
key_terms.الْفِرَاقُ: Separation (of soul from body or loved ones)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'the calf binding to the calf' in Surah Al-Qari'ah according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the verses of Surah Al-Qari'ah by linking the dying person's search for a healer to the inevitable separation from loved ones, while interpreting the 'binding of calf to calf' as the world clinging to the Hereafter. This exegesis highlights the transition from worldly attachment to the final return to the Lord, emphasizing the spiritual reality of death as a decisive shift in existence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Jabir, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Blessed and High [75:27] And it will be Said: Who cast a spell on you? and it is thought that it is the separation’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So if it was that, the death comes upon the son of Adam<sup>as</sup>, he says, ‘Is there one who is a healer (physician)?’
[75:28] And he would think he has separated He would be convinced of separating from the loved ones [75:29] And affliction turns to an affliction.
Heasws said: ‘The world turns to the Hereafter’. [75:30] To your Lord on that day shall be the driving.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘To the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds is the destination’.
en.sarwar: 32. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Jabir who has said the following:
“I asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, ‘And it is said, “Who is able to provide curing charm?”’ (75:28-30)
The Imam said, ‘That is a son of Adam who on facing death says, “Is there a physician?”
“And he finds it to be the departing,” means that he becomes certain about departing his loved ones.’
The Imam then read, ‘When one leg turns around the other,’ means when the present life turns into the life hereafter,
“then it is the time to be driven to your Lord”
means to the Lord of the worlds is the destination.’”
